title: AI this week: the developments that matter
dek: New models, money, lawsuits and rules. A running log of the AI news worth knowing, with what it means for ordinary users.
seoTitle: AI news this week: timeline of key developments
bigLabel: Companies named in a lawsuit filed on 12 Nov that asks a court to freeze advanced AI development

glance.what: In the past ten days Google and Anthropic released new models, Anthropic began marketing its stock market listing, Nvidia's founder was forced out, and nonprofits asked a court to freeze frontier AI. In India, the government released more homegrown models and questioned apps over footage used to train robots.
glance.why: AI is now in phones, offices and government services. Who builds it, who pays for it and what rules apply decide what you can use, what it costs and how safe it is.
glance.next: Nvidia reports earnings on 17 Nov. Anthropic expects to price its IPO on 18 Nov and list on 19 Nov. India's draft AI rules are expected this month.

forYou: Most of this week's launches need nothing from you. Free AI video tools and new models bring a wave of scam apps and fake 'premium' offers, so download only from official app stores and company sites.

events.title: India releases more homegrown AI models
events.summary: The IT ministry announces new models under the IndiaAI Mission: Soket's Eka-1 and ZenteiQ's Dhir 2B and 5B, built for Indian languages and, in some cases, offline use.

events.title: Free AI video in Google Vids
events.summary: Google makes its Omni 1.2 Flash video model available in Google Vids, with three free 15-second clips a month, and cuts the developer price to 7 US cents a second.

events.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
events.summary: Anthropic releases new versions of its top models, saying they improve coding, multi-step reasoning and coordination between AI agents.

events.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon
events.summary: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, mainly for its Ultra subscribers and developers, and expands Gemini features on more Android devices.

events.title: Anthropic starts marketing its IPO
events.summary: Anthropic launches the roadshow for its share sale: 825 million shares at $70–78 each, to list on Nasdaq as 'ANT'. SiliconANGLE reports $17 billion revenue and a $536 million operating loss last quarter. Seven partners, including Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and TSMC, agree to buy $26 billion of shares privately.

events.title: Nonprofits sue to freeze frontier AI
events.summary: Four nonprofits, including Public Citizen, sue Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI in San Francisco, asking a judge to stop them building or releasing more capable AI. They argue the risks break California's unfair competition law. The claims have not been tested in court, no freeze has been ordered, and the companies had not commented.

events.title: TSMC to invest up to $1 billion in AI labs
events.summary: Chipmaker TSMC's board approves up to $1 billion of AI investments, split between OpenAI and Anthropic shares, Ars Technica reports, citing Reuters.

events.title: India asks: is home footage training foreign robots?
events.summary: The IT ministry meets Pronto, Urban Company, Snabbit and robotics firms over video recorded by workers inside Indian homes and whether it is sold to overseas developers of robot AI. Pronto says it keeps only anonymised footage for training.

events.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang is out
events.summary: The founder of the company whose chips power most AI steps down as CEO; reports say the board pushed him out. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Nvidia says its product roadmap continues.
